the signal to noise ratio of a signal modulated on a Poisson process increases as the square root of the number of modulating frequencies, and that the signal to background ratio of the modulated Poisson process is the same as the signal to background for an unmodulated Poisson process.
the power spectrum of a modulated point process has only those frequencies present in the modulating signal.
modulation of the firing rate of a Poisson point process introduces power only for the frequencies contained in the modulating signal.

the results of this paper show that temporal patterning in the discharges of neurons can be used to convey information.
